svg.title: What closing a node does
svg.desc: Animated: two one-edge AGV commands in base_schedule, followed from the reservation loop through DiscreteGarageState, GetStaticFilter and CollisionTable::Query to the boolean masks of GraphFilterProperties that every search reads. The last step shows the gap left by a command that spans several nodes.
svg.metadata: ["base_schedule holds two commands for AGV-1, each one graph edge: c1 W26@90 -> W27@90 and c2 W27@90 -> P24@90. Scheduler-built schedules always look like this: one CHUGG motion per edge, one ActionNode per motion.", "The reservation loop: SetAgvDisabled(1) sets agvs_[1].disabled; SetNodeDisabled adds the source and destination of each command to disabled_nodes_ (a std::set<uint32_t>). W27 is the end of c1 and the start of c2, so the whole route is covered: {24, 26, 27}.", "GetStaticFilter(AGV, ...) copies disabled_nodes_ into all_disabled_nodes and adds the node of every disabled entity (AGV-1 stands on W26). For each node it takes the largest window the node allows (max_resource_size_index; XL here) as a footprint, PAYLOAD + index(XL).", "For each heading of the node it asks the CollisionTable: Query(PAYLOAD + index(XL), AGV, {27, 90}) returns every pose and edge where an AGV would overlap that window. Both go into disabled_poses and disabled_edges.", "All three nodes together: the route, both edges of it and every edge touching its stops are off, plus any pose whose footprint reaches into a window. The graph itself is not edited: Layout, PoseGraph, GarageGraph and CollisionTable stay as they are.", "GraphFilterProperties(gg_, disabled_poses, disabled_edges) builds two boolean masks over the graph, all true, then false for each listed pose and edge. disabledness_filters keeps one per footprint (AGV, TRAY, each payload window); CHUGG builds the same masks as constraints_.", "The gap, a different request: AGV-1 stands on W25 and its one command c W25@90 -> W27@90 passes through W26. Only W25 and W27 are reserved. Their windows block the edges W25-W26 and W26-W27, but the pose W26 and the edge P23-W26 stay on, so a new plan could park an AGV on W26, in the running AGV's way."]

g.text: Nothing is removed from the graph. Closing a node adds its id to a set; every filter built from the state then switches off the poses and edges that touch the node's largest window. Overlaps are drawn
